key_insight: Post-optimization subspace corrections can significantly improve ADAPT-VQE results without growing the ansatz or rerunning nonlinear optimization, cutting both circuit depth and measurement cost.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical path to make quantum chemistry workflows more hardware-efficient by extracting more accuracy from already-optimized states on near-term quantum devices.
method: Apply Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization after ADAPT-VQE optimization.
Use identity-augmented q-sc-EOM to correct truncated or sampled-rank ADAPT-VQE states.
Estimate performance against energy-error and resource-cost thresholds without adding new adaptive layers.
evidence_signal: Across molecular systems up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduced the optimized iterations needed to reach 1.6 mEh by up to about 6× and lowered measurement cost by up to about 40×.
watch_item: The gains depend on the quality of the optimized state and the chosen resource-cost model, so benefits may be smaller for low-entropy systems or noise-prone hardware runs.
paper_title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
